label: D1 after a1->S1 unrewarded; larger when belief still favours S1, late episode
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * belief ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * belief**3 ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * belief_cover ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief**4
explanation: Only active at D1 (zero at GO and D2). Its magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a1 -> S1 common unrewarded (residual about +0.25; every other previous-trial pattern is about -0.03). Within those trials it gets larger when the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good is still high (a steep convex belief**3 term: an unexpected loss at the believed-good state), and it rises later in the episode. It is slightly smaller when the trial before was also unrewarded and when belief_cover is high. On the window first trial, where the previous trial is not in the window, a small belief-weighted term for an unrewarded D1 adds a little. The single a1 S1 u indicator gives dev R^2 beyond timing 0.28; the full 8 terms give dev 0.366 and test 0.376. That matches the all ceiling (0.37) and beats all observed (0.35), so dropping the model value / policy costs essentially nothing here (policy decile alone 0.06, value 0.00). Future and hidden variables (this reward, next choice, good state, since_rev) add about 0. The rest of the variance is large spikes that no additive cue explains, many of them on context trials whose history falls outside the window.
